title: Microsoft Purview: collection policies can filter Insider Risk Management device signals
notes: claim 67: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The device-policy precedence warning, roadmap facts, permissions and PowerShell control are supported by current Microsoft documentation, including the changed deployment page. Microsoft does not substantiate the assurance that end users see no change; the control path and cost rationale also need small clarifications.

The roadmap describes collection policies as scoping classification through SITs and activities for scoped users.

claims.claim: Different Purview solution administrators can create collection policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing collection policies to ensure they detect the activities required by IRM policies.
claims.quote: We recommend reviewing collection policies as they can be created by different Purview solution admins to ensure they are setup to detect the activities required by Insider Risk Management policies

claims.claim: Collection policies filter events ingested into Purview and used by Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: Once ingested, that data can be classified and used by various Microsoft Purview signal consuming solutions, such as Microsoft Purview Activity explorer, Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management

claims.claim: Collection-policy conditions can use sensitive information types, such as Content contains a SIT.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: File copied to removable media is a supported collection-policy activity for devices.
claims.quote: | File copied to removable media | When a file is copied to a removable media, such as a USB flash drive, on an onboarded endpoint device | Devices |

claims.claim: Collection policies filter on the data source as well as conditions and activities.
claims.quote: Collection policies filter events based on: A match to one or more conditions and activities defined in the event. A match to the data source or location where the event is happening.

claims.claim: A configured and deployed device collection policy takes precedence when its filters conflict with what an IRM policy monitors.
claims.quote: if there's a conflict between what the Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor and what the collection policy is configured to filter for, the collection policy configuration takes precedence.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A device activity filtered out by the collection policy is not collected or available for review in IRM, even if the IRM policy monitors it.
claims.quote: if you configure an Insider Risk Management policy to monitor a specific activity for devices, but you configure the collection policy to filter out that device activity, the device activity isn't collected and isn't available for review in Insider Risk Management.

claims.claim: IRM ignores an indicator collected by a collection policy if the IRM policy is not configured for it.
claims.quote: If a collection policy is configured to collect something that an Insider Risk Management policy isn't configured for, then the indicator is collected, but Insider Risk Management ignores it.

claims.claim: The documented precedence effect applies only to device indicators in IRM policies.
claims.quote: This only applies to device indicators in Insider Risk Management policies, and only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented IRM precedence effect occurs only when a device collection policy is deployed.
claims.quote: This only applies to device indicators in Insider Risk Management policies, and only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Purview combines all collection policies for a data source into a single collection policy during back-end evaluation.
claims.quote: on the back end, during policy evaluation, Microsoft Purview combines all the collection policies for a data source into a single collection policy for that data source. So all the conditions for a data source are used when identifying matches.
